title: Concept: Password form submits with GET, placing the secret in the URL
description: A GET form puts every field into the query string, so a password appears in browser history, in the Referer of subsequent requests and in every proxy and access log on the path. The secret then survives the session it belonged to.
applicability: Responses that render a login or password-change form.
risk: The password is written into URLs that are logged, shared and cached, so it persists far longer than the request and leaks to anyone who can read those logs.
